name: Projected Distinguishing Range / Star Number
details: For every finite binary concept class, $\mathrm R^p(\mathcal H)\geq\mathrm S(\mathcal H)$.
proof: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_s$ and $h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_s$ witness an $s$-star.  Project to $T=\{x_1,\ldots,x_s\}$.  In $\mathcal H_{|T}$, $h_i$ differs from the center $h_0$ exactly at $x_i$.  Any coordinate set whose traces distinguish every projected concept must therefore contain every $x_i$, or it fails to distinguish $h_0$ from $h_i$.  Thus $\mathrm R(\mathcal H_{|T})\geq s$; maximizing over $T$ proves $\mathrm R^p\geq\mathrm S$.
witness_verification: For half-intervals, projected distinguishing range is $n-1$, while the star number is $2$.
